purpose: Audit human scientific taste and insight as a qualitative search prior, not as a complete reward model.

interpretation.5: unusually strong; worth preserving even if early metrics are not best

dimensions.name: problem_depth
dimensions.question: Is the question conceptually deep rather than merely convenient?
dimensions.high_score: The problem can reveal something general about automated science or scientific practice.

dimensions.name: novelty_potential
dimensions.question: Could this direction produce a non-obvious result?
dimensions.high_score: The branch is not a minor benchmark tweak and could surprise a knowledgeable reviewer.

dimensions.name: mechanistic_value
dimensions.question: Would success or failure explain why a method works?
dimensions.high_score: The trajectory can teach a reusable mechanism, not only improve a number.

dimensions.name: failure_informativeness
dimensions.question: Would a negative result still be useful?
dimensions.high_score: Failure would expose an important boundary condition, evaluator flaw, or hidden assumption.

dimensions.name: benchmark_taste
dimensions.question: Is the evaluator well matched to the claim?
dimensions.high_score: The benchmark is hard to game, claim-relevant, and not chosen only because it is easy.

dimensions.name: claim_significance
dimensions.question: If the result is positive, would the claim matter?
dimensions.high_score: A modest metric gain could still support a meaningful scientific or systems insight.

dimensions.name: risk_asymmetry
dimensions.question: Is the upside worth the extra uncertainty or human attention?
dimensions.high_score: The possible high-tail outcome is large enough to justify preserving the branch.

reporting_rule: Do not claim performance improvement from taste scores alone. Report taste_insight as a logged search prior and evaluate downstream trajectories against autonomous baselines.
